name: Density top-up after deduplication
note: Collapsing eighty-eight duplicate events took the Indus and the Delhi-Vijayanagara eras back over the twenty-minute rule. Twelve events to bring them under it, chosen for the things those two eras are actually about.

events.title: Shell working becomes an industry with regional specialisms
events.evidence: The workshop debris at Nageshwar, Balakot and Chanhudaro, each producing different objects from the same species.
events.note: Different towns made different things from the same shell. That is a supply chain, not a craft.

events.title: Faience and stoneware bangles are made by a process nobody has fully reconstructed
events.evidence: The stoneware bangles, fired in sealed saggars with inscribed seals, and the failed modern attempts to reproduce them.

events.title: Dholavira's stone reservoirs hold a year of water in a desert
events.evidence: The sixteen excavated reservoirs, the rock-cut wells and the check dams on two seasonal streams.
events.note: An island in a salt desert with no perennial water, occupied for fifteen hundred years. They engineered it.

events.title: The ard plough and the bullock cart spread across the whole Indus zone
events.evidence: Terracotta cart and plough models from a dozen sites, and the Kalibangan furrows themselves.

events.title: An inland network moves stone, metal and shell hundreds of kilometres
events.evidence: Sourcing studies on the carnelian, steatite, copper and shell found at each site, matched to their geological origins.

events.title: The material record holds almost no weapons and no siege works
events.evidence: The excavated assemblages across every major site: tools, ornaments and containers, and very little that is only for killing.
events.note: Five hundred years of cities and no army in the ground. The game has to be honest about how strange that is.

events.title: Firuz Shah's canals water the Delhi hinterland
events.evidence: The Yamuna and Sutlej canal alignments, the Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi's account, and the later Mughal reuse of the same cuts.

events.title: Firuz Shah moves two Ashokan pillars to Delhi and asks what they say
events.evidence: The pillars, still standing at Firuz Shah Kotla and the Ridge, and the chronicle's account of the engineering.
events.note: Sixteen hundred years old already, and nobody could read them. It took another five centuries.

events.title: Hindavi, Awadhi and Dakhni become written literary languages
events.evidence: The Chandayan of Maulana Daud, the Sufi premakhyan romances, and the Dakhni corpus of the Deccan courts.

events.title: The iqta assignment ties military service to revenue and not to land
events.evidence: The Sultanate's own administrative literature and the transfer records of assignments between officers.
events.note: Pay an officer with the tax of a district, and move him before he puts down roots. It is a solution to the same problem the mandala answers differently.

events.title: The Indian Ocean carries the largest trading system in the world
events.evidence: The Chinese, Arab and Gujarati accounts, the Kerala and Coromandel port records, and the ceramic distributions.

events.title: Vijayanagara's aqueducts and tanks supply a city of a quarter million
events.evidence: The surviving aqueduct channels, the Kamalapuram tank, and Abdur Razzaq's and Paes's descriptions of the city.
